comments.body:
Evidence (2026-11-03, read-only: `aws --profile frontier` + SSM AWS-RunShellScript on i-00880b2c7f13527c5)

Current state
- CloudWatch Logs: 22 groups in the account, none for the rebar host (all lmn-*, snap-demo, bedrock, bakeoff). Gap unchanged since the incident.
- Host: Amazon Linux 2023, aarch64. No CloudWatch agent (no /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent, unit inactive), no fluent-bit/vector/rsyslog/journal-upload.
- Instance role rebar-gerrit-cloudwatch-basic ALREADY grants logs:CreateLogGroup/CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents on * (iam.tf, S1 commit 30c92d4f43d, comment "push instance metrics + ship logs"). No logs:PutRetentionPolicy / DescribeLogStreams.
- journald: persistent (/var/log/journal), SystemMaxUse 3 GiB (99-rebar-disk-ceiling.conf), full at 3.0G. Oldest retained boot starts 2026-09-06 02:43 UTC, so the 2026-09-04 incident window is already gone from the on-box journal too.
- All compose containers (gerrit, review-bot, opcert, rebar-mcp) use the journald log driver, so journald holds the rebar services' output. nginx is NOT in journald: it writes /var/log/nginx/{access,error}.log (logrotate daily).
- Volume, last 24h: about 5.8 MB of journal message text (~55k entries; top: docker.service/containers, audit, init.scope, rebar-autodeploy, refresh-policy-routes, rebar-health); kernel about 0.09 MB; nginx error.log about 0.09 MB/day, access.log about 3.5 MB/day.
- Console: `get-console-output --latest` returns a CURRENT snapshot (timestamp 2026-11-04T03:58Z, 64 KiB) on this Nitro instance; the "2 days stale" reading came from the non-latest cached form. Serial console access is disabled at the account level.

Vendor facts
- CloudWatch agent journald input exists only from v1.300070.0 (released 2026-08-19, PR aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent#2121; issue #382 had been open for years). AL2023's dnf repo still ships 1.300067.1 (no journald). The SSM Distributor package AmazonCloudWatchAgent is at 1.300074.1.

Root cause of the missing off-box path
- S1 (2026-06-29) granted log-shipping IAM intent, and S2 routed every container to journald, but no story owned installing a shipper or creating a log group. At that time the CloudWatch agent could not read journald at all, and the host's metrics went through `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data` in observability.sh instead, so logs never acquired an owner. Nothing checks that host logs reach CloudWatch, so the absence was silent.
- GerritReachable is also probed from the host itself; the only non-host observations today are the EC2 status checks.

Design choices with no prior intent are pending an operator decision (install source for a journald-capable agent, external probe kind, nginx access-log inclusion); see session report.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The 2026-09-04 21:28 UTC Gerrit outage left no evidence. The host (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, tag `Name=rebar-gerrit`) has no off-box log destination: no CloudWatch agent is installed and no log group exists (2026-11-03 survey, see comment). Every health signal except the EC2 status checks originates on the host itself, so a dead host silences its own observer. Restarting the host destroys the only forensic state.

Root cause: S1 (`infra/terraform/iam.tf` `cloudwatch_basic`, "push instance metrics + ship logs") granted log-write IAM, and S2 routed every container to journald (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` `logging: driver: journald`). No story ever owned a shipper or a log group. The CloudWatch agent could not read journald until v1.300070.0 (2026-08-19), and nothing checks that host logs arrive off-box, so the gap stayed silent.

## Approach

All of it is AWS-managed and Terraform-declared. The repo adds no installer code, no RPM download and no version pin, and does not touch `install-observability.sh` or `autodeploy.sh`.

- **Agent install:** an `aws_ssm_association` running `AWS-ConfigureAWSPackage` (`action=Install`, `name=AmazonCloudWatchAgent`, version unpinned) targets `tag:Name=rebar-gerrit` on `rate(1 day)`, so a rebuilt host is covered with no manual step. The Distributor package's default version is 1.300074.1, which is journald-capable (>= 1.300070.0). Re-running at the same version is a no-op success (amazon-ssm-agent `agent/plugins/configurepackage/configurepackage.go` `checkAlreadyInstalled`).
- **Agent config:** an `aws_ssm_parameter` `AmazonCloudWatch-rebar-gerrit-host` holds `infra/terraform/cwagent/rebar-host.json`. A second association running `AmazonCloudWatch-ManageAgent` (`action=configure`, `mode=ec2`, `optionalConfigurationSource=ssm`, `optionalConfigurationLocation=<param>`, `optionalRestart=yes`; names confirmed with `describe-document`) applies it on `rate(1 hour)`.
- **Config content:** journald collect_list entries for the kernel (`matches: [{"_TRANSPORT":"kernel"}]`), `docker.service` (all 4 containers log there; confirmed `_SYSTEMD_UNIT=docker.service` for gerrit, review-bot, opcert and rebar-mcp), `rebar-*` units, `nginx.service` and `init.scope` (systemd's unit-failure lines). Plus a `files` entry for `/var/log/nginx/error.log` only, never `access.log`. Everything goes to one log group with a per-source stream `{instance_id}/<source>`. `run_as_user=root`, no metrics section, and no `retention_in_days` (Terraform owns retention).
- **Log group:** `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` `/rebar/gerrit-host`, `retention_in_days = 90`, matching `bedrock_spend_cap.tf` and `monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf`.
- **IAM:** a new role policy on `rebar-gerrit-instance-role` grants `logs:CreateLogStream`, `logs:PutLogEvents` and `logs:DescribeLogStreams` on that group's ARN only, plus `ssm:GetParameter` on that one parameter ARN. The actions mirror the live `CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy`, minus metrics/X-Ray/retention.
- **Shipping-stopped alarm (AC5):** an alarm on `AWS/Logs IncomingLogEvents` (`LogGroupName`) with Sum < 1 over 3x300s, `datapoints_to_alarm = 3`, `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, sent to the existing SNS topic.
- **External observer (AC2):** an `aws_route53_health_check` (HTTPS, `var.dns_name`, `/config/server/version`, port 443), plus an alarm on `AWS/Route53 HealthCheckStatus` (Minimum < 1, 3x60s, breaching).
- **Runbook:** `infra/runbooks/gerrit-host-wedged-ssm-lost.md` gains (a) a capture step before any restart: `aws ec2 get-console-output --latest` saved to disk, about 1 minute; and (b) an "alarm to evidence" path reading `/rebar/gerrit-host` with `aws logs tail` and Logs Insights, which needs no live host.

## Scope

- `infra/terraform/host_logs.tf` (new): log group, parameter, 2 associations, IAM policy, both alarms, health check.
- `infra/terraform/cwagent/rebar-host.json` (new): the agent config.
- `tests/infra/test_host_logs_offbox.py` (new): offline contract tests.
- `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`, `tests/unit/test_alarm_window_tuning.py`, `tests/unit/test_alarm_description_byte_limit.py`: raise the alarm-count floors by 2.
- `infra/runbooks/gerrit-host-wedged-ssm-lost.md`: the capture step and the evidence path.

Out of scope: a memory alarm (`witted-invisible-roan`), `autodeploy.sh`, the MCP compose files, and narrowing the pre-existing `cloudwatch_basic` wildcard.

## Testing

Written first and failing before the fix:
- The config JSON parses. It ships the kernel via `_TRANSPORT=kernel`, `docker.service`, `rebar-*`, `nginx.service` and nginx `error.log`. It never references `access.log`. Every log_group_name equals the Terraform group, and no entry sets `retention_in_days`.
- Terraform declares the log group with `retention_in_days = 90`. The parameter name starts with `AmazonCloudWatch-` and loads the JSON file. The install association uses `AmazonCloudWatchAgent` with no `version` and a `schedule_expression`. Both associations target `tag:Name`.
- The IAM policy's logs resources are the group ARN, not `*`, and `ssm:GetParameter` is scoped to the parameter ARN.
- The IncomingLogEvents alarm and the HealthCheckStatus alarm treat missing data as breaching, with `datapoints_to_alarm == evaluation_periods`, and both have `alarm_actions`.
- Seeded negative: a config that adds `access.log`, or drops the kernel match, fails the checker helper.
- The runbook contains `get-console-output` with `--latest` before any restart instruction, and names `/rebar/gerrit-host`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 - `pytest tests/infra/test_host_logs_offbox.py` passes, and failed on the pre-fix tree.
- [x] AC2 - `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass in `infra/terraform`. A read-only `terraform plan -lock=false` shows only additions: log group, parameter, 2 associations, role policy, health check and 2 alarms.
- [x] AC3 - `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the 3 alarm-contract test modules pass.
- [x] AC4 - The runbook documents the pre-restart console capture (expected added downtime about 1 minute) and the off-box evidence path, stating that the 2026-09-04 window is unrecoverable: no off-box copy existed, and the on-box journal's oldest entry is 2026-09-06.
- [ ] AC5 [non-codebase] - After an operator `terraform apply`, `aws logs tail /rebar/gerrit-host --profile frontier` shows kernel, docker and nginx-error streams. After an agent stop, the last lines remain readable and the IncomingLogEvents alarm enters ALARM within 15 minutes.
      provenance: environment=prod account 896586841071 us-east-1; principal=operator frontier profile; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — only a live apply and agent stop exercise the shipping path and its alarm.
- [x] AC6 [non-codebase] - The Route 53 health check reports Healthy, and its alarm is OK while Gerrit serves and independent of `rebar/host` publishing.
      provenance: environment=prod account 896586841071 us-east-1; principal=operator frontier profile; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — 2026-11-04 after apply of c790f07f0b2: health check d9a1a8c3-21a7-5102-09de-24fedb23fadd, all 16 checkers "Success: HTTP Status Code 200"; rebar-gerrit-external-probe-down OK since 14:53:25 PST.
